reason: E1 shows that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves ductility in RHEAs, but it does not involve Ti or the specific NbMoTaW system. E2 only provides general background on NbMoTaW and does not mention Ti, inverted microstructures, or irradiation resistance. The key premises about Ti inducing the inverted microstructure, the specific mechanism, and the preservation of high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Ti addition to NbMoTaW can form an 'inverted' BCC+B2 microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves room-temperature ductility while maintaining high yield strength.
The mechanism involves improved grain boundary cohesion and crack deflection due to Ti-modified interfacial chemistry.
The modified alloy will maintain high-temperature yield strength (~400 MPa at 1600°C) and irradiation resistance.
